title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: this is part of the long computation in 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (a continuation of La Longue Marche). The groups appear to be profinite, related to the Teichmüller-type group/GT setting. The objects are triples (u,a,b), with u in a group like Ẑ (or Ĝ) and a, b in groups N'_ρ, N'_σ. Here τ, τ' are involution-like elements and ε_2, ε_3, χ are ±1-valued characters. The page title says 502; the archive number is 596.

From the previous page: E := S_0^Π Γ^!_{ρ,σ} is a central extension 1→μ→E→Z^!_{ρ,σ}→1 with μ={±1}. Over two index-2 subgroups Z^{!'} and Z^{!'''} the restricted extensions E' = S_0^ΠΓ^{!'} and E''' = S_0^ΠΓ^{!'''} are split. The splittings are given by explicit subgroups H' = S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'} and H''' = S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'''}, which are the elements congruent mod Π_0. So E' ≅ H'×μ and E''' ≅ H'''×μ (formula 68). The goal is to decide whether the extension E itself is trivial.

On this page Grothendieck asks whether H' and H''' are normal in E. The marginal note says they are subgroups of index 4 in S_0^ΠΓ_{ρ,σ}. If H' is normal, E/H' is a group of order 4 containing μ. Then E 'comes from' an extension of Z^!/Z^{!'} ≅ ±1 by μ, compatible with the given splitting. One would then decide whether that order-4 group is Z/4 or (Z/2)^2.

He reduces normality to one test. H' is normal in E' (it is a complement to the central μ, and E' = H'×μ). E' has index 2 in E. So H' is normal in E iff it is normalized by a single x ∈ E∖E'.

Case 1° (H' in E). He chooses x = (u_0,a_0,b_0) with u_0 = τ, so ε_3(u_0) = ε_2(u_0) = χ(u_0) = −1. He takes α_0 = τ, β_0 = 1, giving a_0 = τ' and b_0 = τ, so x = (τ, τ', τ). A crossed-out first attempt (x = τ) was rejected as not lying in the right group.

The next page completes the test. Conjugating (u,a,b) ∈ H' by x gives (τ(u), τ'(a), τ(b)). This lies in H' iff τ'(a) ≡ τ(a) mod Π_0, which comes down to ε_2(u) = 1. That is not implied by ε_3(u) = 1, so H' is not normal. He then starts the analogous test for H'''.

General principle: conjugation by x sends the complement H' to another complement of μ in E'. The two differ by a homomorphism Z^{!'}→μ, and H' is normal iff that homomorphism is trivial. Here the homomorphism is ε_2 restricted to Z^{!'}.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page.

In (70) the intermediate formula a_0 = ε_{3,0}(τ')α_0^{-1}u_0 with α_0 = u_0 = τ gives α_0^{-1}u_0 = 1. So a_0 = τ' only if ε_{3,0}(τ') denotes the element τ' itself (or acts as such). The notation is ambiguous but the result x = (τ, τ', τ) is consistent with the next page.

The statement that normality of H' would make the extension 'come from' an extension of Z^!/Z^{!'} by μ is only heuristic ('grosso modo'). It also needs compatibility with the splitting; Grothendieck signals this himself.

ideas.what: Testing triviality of a central ±1-extension that is split on two index-2 subgroups, by asking whether the splitting subgroups are normal and then reducing to an order-4 quotient
ideas.modern_name: Elementary cohomology of central extensions: H^2(G,Z/2), restriction to index-2 subgroups, complements of a central subgroup differing by homomorphisms (H^1)

ideas.what: Normality of an index-2-normal subgroup reduced to normalization by one coset representative x = (τ, τ', τ), computed explicitly through characters ε_2, ε_3, χ
Underlying object: a sign (±1) extension of a profinite group Z^!_{ρ,σ} appearing in the analysis of the 'équation des lacets' (relations of Teichmüller/GT type)
ideas.modern_name: possibly related to sign or central-extension issues in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group / braid-type relations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara (GT); Grothendieck's own program in Esquisse
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (circulated 1981), only in general form

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine step in a long explicit computation: checking whether two splitting subgroups of a central ±1 extension are normal. The method is elementary group theory. The page's interest lies only in its place within the unpublished 'équation des lacets' manuscript, not in any new result here.
transcription_corrections: The superscripts read Γ^{!'} and Γ^{!'''} (one and three primes, as on the previous page), not Γ^{!!} and Γ^{!!!}. Likewise Z^{!'} and Z^{!'''}.
Marginal note: 'SS-groupes d'indice 4 dans S_0^Π Γ_{ρ,σ}' (sous-groupes of index 4).
'(grosso modo dans un quelconque [?] par ces sous-groupes)' probably reads '(grosso modo, en passant au quotient par ces sous-groupes)'.
'qu'il faudrait ensuite construire' is likely 'qu'il faudrait ensuite connaître/déterminer (comme triviale ou non triviale)'.
The crossed-out line in (70) reads 'x = τ, qui n'est pas dans S_0^ΠΓ^!'.
Bottom line: 'donc x = (u_0 = τ, a_0 = τ', b_0 = τ)'; the word under (70) is 'donc'.
The point 'est normalisé par x' is phrased as 'signifie simplement qu'il est normalisé par x'.
